column2: era auto-detect calls `gh` / `_ground_truth_calibration_incentive_shipped` without resolving an `owner/repo` string. with `issues=[]` and `repo=none`, the shipped check always returns `calibration_incentive_check_unavailable`, so auto-boundary degrades even when `gh` works. worse, resolving repo from the consumer clone’s git toplevel (or ambient `gh` default) can query the wrong repository for incentive issue #5461, which lives on the plugin source repo (`character-ai/larch`), not necessarily the cwd checkout.

reusing `_ground_truth_calibration_incentive_shipped` / `_incentive_issue_from_gh` alone cannot produce an era cutoff. the shipped helper returns only `(bool, str)` with no boundary datetime. `_incentive_issue_from_gh` fetches only `state,statereason,closedbypullrequestsreferences`, omitting `closedat` (needed for the cutoff) and `labels`/`body` (needed for `_has_not_planned_signal`). an implementer can pass the shipped gate yet still have no authoritative boundary, causing wrong pre/post splits or silent fallback.

the plan takes the post-era boundary from issue close/merge time but does not define behavior when a shipped-shaped #5461 payload lacks a parseable `closedat`. failure modes cover malformed json and closed-without-pr, not this case. an implementer may guess a timestamp (e.g. from pr refs or `updated_at`) and mis-segment corpora.

plan failure modes require argparse-style exit `2` for malformed `--era-since-date`. reusing `analyze_issues._parse_ground_truth_since_date` raises `systemexit` with default exit `1` and `error=invalid --since-date`, which may not match the documented contract.

the planned single-fetch `gh issue view --json` field list omits `number`, but auto-boundary passes `issues=[payload]` into `_ground_truth_calibration_incentive_shipped`, which builds `_merged_issue_index` via `issue_number(issue)` (`issue["number"]` required). without `number`, auto era detection raises `keyerror` inside `_merged_issue_index`, or lookup misses and falls back to `_incentive_issue_from_gh` (a second fetch omitting `closedat`/labels/body), breaking the one-fetch boundary contract and yielding boundary-unavailable or wrong shipped results even when #5461 is closed-with-pr and the first response was valid.

the auto-boundary path only degrades on a non-zero `gh` exit or json parse failure. a missing `gh` executable raises `filenotfounderror` before those branches, so the planned no-`gh` test will traceback instead of rendering the required boundary-unavailable markdown. `/voter-calibration --era` fails anywhere `gh` is not on path, leaving the fallback path unshipped and making required no-`gh` coverage impossible to pass.

primary repo resolution uses `git -c <plugin_root> config`, but the fallback `gh repo view --json namewithowner` is only described as "scoped to `plugin_root`" without a mechanism. invoking `gh` from the consumer clone cwd can resolve the wrong `owner/repo` and query #5461 on a non-plugin repository. in the common skill path the operator runs `/voter-calibration` from a consumer clone while `plugin_root` is the plugin tree. if `plugin_root` lacks `remote.origin.url` and the fallback runs unscoped, `gh repo view` resolves the consumer repo, `gh issue view 5461 --repo <consumer>` can return a different issue #5461, and auto era boundary comes from the wrong close time or a misleading shipped gate.

the binding scope asks for segmented agreement plus severity scoreboards. the plan narrows rendering to reusing `_render` scoreboard sections per corpus slice and `--era all` copy only calls out high rate and calibration score. an implementer can ship era mode with severity tables only and miss the agreement readout the feature explicitly requested.

the plan adds pre-boundary, post-boundary, and missing-`started_at` manifests and lists `--era all|pre|post` invocations, but only mandates exclusion counting and gh-boundary cases. wrong bucketing (e.g. keyed on basename or mis-resolved `run_dir`) can still pass malformed-date and missing-`started_at` tests while corpora are merged or swapped.

`_resolve_incentive_repo` must not call `_detect_repo()`. the plan points implementers at `_detect_repo()` slug rules, but that helper always runs unscoped `gh repo view` before `git config` (`python/analyze_issues.py:3399-3407`). calling or importing it revives consumer-cwd wrong-repo resolution for #5461 despite the plugin-root-only contract.

passing `repo=` into `_ground_truth_calibration_incentive_shipped` keeps a hidden second `gh` fetch. when `issues=[payload]` does not index #5461 (wrong/missing number, stub mismatch), `_ground_truth_calibration_incentive_shipped` still calls `_incentive_issue_from_gh` because `repo` is set. that second fetch omits `closedat`/`labels`/`body`, can still mark shipped, and breaks the one-fetch boundary contract the plan documents.

defensive number inject uses the wrong dict spread order. the plan injects `{"number": ground_truth_verdict_incentive_issue_number, **payload}`. because `**payload` wins, any wrong number already in the stub/gh json is kept, lookup for #5461 misses, and the repo fallback path above can fire.

repo-unresolved harness does not say how to isolate `plugin_root`. the script only resolves `plugin_root` from `claude_plugin_root` or `parents[3]`. under `env -u claude_plugin_root` the harness still points at the real larch checkout, which has `remote.origin.url`, so the planned repo-unresolved case may never run and `gh` may still be invoked.

`_resolve_incentive_repo` does not mirror the `gh` `filenotfounderror` degradation contract. the plan wraps only `_run_gh_json` for missing `gh` (`filenotfounderror` → boundary unavailable, exit `0`). `_resolve_incentive_repo` runs `git -c <plugin_root> config` and only lists "subprocess failure" as a soft failure. a missing `git` binary raises `filenotfounderror` before returncode handling, so `/voter-calibration --era` can traceback on auto-boundary instead of the documented unavailable-boundary markdown path.

the no-gh coverage can miss the intended `filenotfounderror` branch. if the test removes `gh` by blanking path, `git -c <plugin_root> config` can fail first and the new missing-gh path is never exercised, so the recovery branch stays unverified.

planned acceptance readout documents only the manual `--era-since-date` workflow. issue scope makes shipped-with-pr auto-boundary the default and manual cutoff the override when incentive is not yet shipped. the planned skill note only tells operators to run `--era all --era-since-date yyyy-mm-dd`, so the primary post-ship acceptance path (`--era all` with auto `closedat`) is undocumented and operators may keep passing manual dates or think era mode is unavailable without them.

era-mode partition greps require pre/post voter isolation, but the plan and harness do not pin exact `## ...` heading strings. implementer-chosen titles can diverge from harness `awk`/grep delimiters, yielding flaky tests, false passes (global grep), or false failures.

the harness bullets describe pre/post/missing `started_at` fixtures but only show tsv paths; `test-voter-calibration.sh` today writes no `manifest.json`. `_ground_truth_run_started_at_strict` reads `<run_dir>/manifest.json`, so without explicit fixture steps every run is excluded, partition greps fail, and era mode cannot be validated.

the plan adds `filenotfounderror` handling in `_resolve_incentive_repo`, but the harness only exercises missing `gh`, repo-unresolved, and missing-`closedat` cases. a regression in the missing-`git` branch can still traceback and ship undetected.
